Significance Recent research on the modern Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) has unveiled a complex three-dimensional structure.
However, most previous studies on the glacial AMOC have primarily concentrated on features associated with two-dimensional overturning.

This study investigates the three-dimensional glacial AMOC by combining sedimentary 231 Pa/ 230 Th reconstructions with model simulations, revealing a substantially intensified Eastern Pathway (EP), which transports Glacial North Atlantic Intermediate Water (GNAIW) from subpolar to subtropical North Atlantic in the eastern basin.

This study investigates the three-dimensional glacial AMOC by combining sedimentary 231 Pa/ 230 Th reconstructions with model simulations, revealing a substantially intensified Eastern Pathway (EP), which transports Glacial North Atlantic Intermediate Water (GNAIW) from subpolar to subtropical North Atlantic in the eastern basin.
The elucidation of this dramatic change of the EP provides a more accurate view of the glacial AMOC and its transport of energy and water properties.

At PD, NADW consists of a mixture of the Labrador Sea Water (LSW) and the overflow waters from the Greenland-Iceland-Norwegian (GIN) Seas and is transported from the subpolar to subtropical North Atlantic through different pathways.

Furthermore, recent studies based on Argo data ( 15 ), ocean reanalysis ( 16 ), and models with a hierarchy of resolutions ( 17 ) suggest that a significant portion of NADW is transported from the subpolar region to the subtropics in the Eastern Pathway (EP) east of MAR at mid-latitude that is steered by surface winds ( 17 ).
Here, we study this question using an ocean general circulation model, iPOP2 ( Materials and Methods ), that simulates the EP at PD in agreement with observations ( 17 ).
We find that the EP was greatly intensified at the LGM, resulting in opposite 231 Pa/ 230 Th changes between the eastern and western Atlantic consistent with reconstructions.

There is also a possibility that the open ocean convection in the glacial North Atlantic simulated in the 3°, and even the 1°, simulations might be biased.
Therefore, the open ocean convection in the LGM subpolar North Atlantic might be a robust feature of the LGM ocean state.

Nevertheless, it is certainly desirable in the future to perform the simulations to explore the open ocean convection and its associated rim currents in more advanced models with higher resolution and, even better, without the hydrostatic approximation that is adopted in the current generation of CESM.

Both 231 Pa and 230 Th are produced at relatively uniform rates in the ocean with a production ratio of 0.093, and the isotopes are subject to ocean transport and particle scavenging ( 67 ).
However, in addition to ocean transport, sediment 231 Pa/ 230 Th can also be influenced by particle flux and composition ( 68 ).

Following the criteria set by a previous compilation of available North Atlantic 231 Pa/ 230 Th sediment core observations ( 6 ), sediment records that were considered to have a dominant influence by particle fluxes were not included in the model-observation comparison in this study ( SI Appendix , Table S1 ).
231 Pa/ 230 Th in iPOP2 is implemented in two versions: p-coupled and p-fixed ( 50 ).
In p-coupled 231 Pa/ 230 Th, the particle fluxes associated with reversible scavenging are simultaneously calculated from the biogeochemical model.
In p-fixed 231 Pa/ 230 Th, the particle fluxes are fixed at the PD values produced by the biogeochemical model in iPOP2.
